A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EEVPD-based tuning work, despite the changed title and format. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V2 reports original sampling experiments, including dimensionality scaling, numerical bias measurements, Bayesian benchmark results, and an EEVPD ablation.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds lattice field-theory evaluations, a distribution-tail sensitivity study, and tuning-convergence measurements.

M1.justification: The EEVPD-based step-size procedure and Algorithm 1 retain the same updates and weighting scheme, moving from Appendix D.2 to Appendix E. Momentum-length adaptation and diagonal preconditioning were already discussed in v2; their expanded description does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: V3 adds interacting scalar phi^4 and U(1) gauge-field sampling tasks, extending evaluation beyond the retained Bayesian and independent-product targets. Appendix C also adds Student-t and generalized-normal target families to examine different tail conditions.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments preserve their comparator sets, including aLMC/MALT, aMCLMC, NUTS, and grid-search uLMC. The new field-theory comparisons use previously evaluated samplers; adjusted HMC, reported for U(1), already appears in v2 Figure 2.

E3.justification: New protocols include controlled physical couplings and Fourier-power errors for phi^4, beta=2 and Polyakov-loop errors for U(1), and 100-dimensional tail sweeps at EEVPD=10^-3 with 50-million-step chains. The retained Bayesian benchmarks keep their error thresholds and EEVPD targets.

E4.justification: Appendix C/Figure 7 adds a systematic investigation of how heavier and lighter tails affect the Gaussian-derived bias bound. Section 6.1 also adds EEVPD autocorrelation and convergence diagnostics. The earlier EEVPD ablation and funnel case study remain, rather than being replaced by these analyses.

E5.justification: V3 specifies that the new 1024^2-dimensional phi^4 experiment uses only two chains because of GPU capacity. The retained benchmarks still use at least 128 chains and 100 bootstrap resamples, with unchanged Table 4 uncertainties. This is new experiment-specific run information, not a reduction in repetitions of an earlier experiment.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and uncertainty tables retain their values. New phi^4 results report 1,344 gradient calls for uMCLMC, 39,240 for aMCLMC, and 133,266 for NUTS. New U(1) results report 198, 15,578, 17,699, and 127,875 for uMCLMC, aMCLMC, adjusted HMC, and NUTS respectively. Figure 7 additionally reports tail-dependent bias, including an exceedance of the Gaussian reference at Student-t nu=3.

T1.justification: The Gaussian bounds, covariance-error lemmas, supporting proofs, and bias–variance derivation remain unchanged after matching renumbered content. Appendices F.2–F.3 add mathematical definitions of the field actions and gauge-invariant observables, including the Polyakov-loop relationship to static potential. No new general bias theorem is established.

C1.justification: The central automatic-tuning and Gaussian-bound contributions remain. The abstract and conclusion now explicitly claim demonstrated effectiveness on million-dimensional statistical and quantum field models. V2's speculative extension to Bayesian neural networks with minibatching noise is dropped.

C2.justification: V2's brief smaller-step validation advice becomes a detailed diagnostic proposal in Section 8, alongside new discussions of conditioning, tails, and bound failures. Section 6 adds explanations of rapid EEVPD estimation and its difference from acceptance-rate tuning. However, Section 8's statement that long tails do not increase bias overgeneralizes Figure 7, which shows a substantial increase for the heaviest tested Student-t case.

D1.justification: V3 supplies field-model couplings, boundary conditions, observable computations, and NVIDIA A100/AMD EPYC hardware information. Code-access information remains equivalent. Conversely, v2 Appendix D.3's explicit disclosure that NUTS supplies the common diagonal preconditioner is no longer stated clearly; the broader prerun discussion does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V3 adds field-theory and diagnostic references, including Albergo et al., Kanwar et al., Vierhaus, and Gelman–Rubin. Appendix F.1 newly distinguishes its sequential-chain evaluation from Hoffman–Sountsov's many-short-chains setting. The central positioning as practical automatic tuning of existing unadjusted samplers remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and conclusion are rewritten. Tuning gains subsections, experimental setup moves into the main text, limitations become a separate section, and the appendices are substantially reorganized into tuning, model details, further experiments, and reproducibility sections.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference main text. V3 adds Figures 5–7, adds tuning-method subheaders to benchmark tables, and relocates the conversion and covariance-result tables to the appendices. Existing tuning and ablation figures are retained as Figures 8–9 within the reorganized layout.

improvement.justification: V2's dimensional-scaling evidence chiefly concerned independent-product targets. V3's interacting field-theory evaluations, with physically relevant observables, substantially strengthen evidence for the central practical scalability claim. Tail-sensitivity experiments and concrete bias diagnostics also make applicability easier to assess. These gains outweigh limited weaknesses: the largest phi^4 test has only two chains, and the new blanket interpretation of long-tail behavior is inconsistent with Figure 7.
